| [CLAIM-302](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-302.md) | Equivalence under feasible tests can be much coarser than statistical equivalence: there are ensembles almost disjoint from uniform that no polynomial-size test tells apart from it, and efficiently samplable ensembles of this kind exist if pseudorandom generators do | A15's witness for "Complexity changes what we mean by an observable", which the owner asked to have developed at U15, corrected by the reading of Goldreich (NOTE of 2026-10-15). The separation itself is unconditional: a counting argument gives ensembles supported on at most 2^(n/2) strings that no circuit of size 2^(n/8) tells from uniform. Only an efficiently samplable witness needs an assumption, and a secure pseudorandom generator supplies one. All of it is asymptotic, about ensembles indexed by n. | Active |
| [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md) | Filing an argument moves work across time: it is paid for now, in filing, indexing, tracking dependencies and checking it is still current, against reconstruction later, so it is worth its cost only when expected reuse covers it, and recurrence is evidence of reuse, not the criterion | A11, at the owner's request for "content to the effect of computation-storage tradeoffs". A11's four expenditures (materialization, indexing, dependency tracking, refresh) and its break-even condition. The arithmetic is trivial. The thesis is about the record: that its second-occurrence rule ([ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)) and the nucleation threshold of [CLAIM-185](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md) are approximations to this trade, and can fail in both directions. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-304](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-304.md) | A rendering can keep a distinction recoverable in principle and make it infeasible to recover: if pseudorandom generators exist, a uniformly random bit can be encoded so that an unbounded receiver recovers it except with probability at most 2⁻⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾, while no efficient receiver does non-negligibly better than chance | A14's first failure mode, computational inaccessibility, and A18's fourth candidate: "Recoverable in principle ≠ recoverable within budget." | [CLAIM-305](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-305.md) | Resolving a singularity by blow-up reparametrizes the states and adds no observation, so it cannot make indistinguishable states distinguishable: every point over a singular point gives the same distribution, and the Fisher information can stay degenerate there; what the resolution buys is a normal form for the divergence, and so the learning coefficient | The owner's LEGO monograph says, in Part I (chapters 4, 6, 7, 9, the Overview and "Definitions and Theorems"), that blow-up "restores identifiability", "introduces new observables" and makes the Fisher information non-degenerate, and maps it onto splitting a LEGO bin. The pulled-back model is p(x \| π(u)), a function of u only through π(u), so every point of the exceptional divisor gives the distribution of the singular point. In p(x \| a, b) = N(ab, 1), the chart a = u, b = uv gives mean u²v and a Fisher matrix of zero all along u = 0. Splitting a bin is refining the observable, which can separate states. [MOM-CLM-099](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-099.md) records that the monograph uses "blow-up" in three senses; this records why the analogy cannot hold in any of them. | Active |
| [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md) | Under a deadline, search can establish presence by finding one item but absence only by exhausting the collection, so "If I can't find it, it isn't there" acts on an unfinished search as negation as failure acts on a finished one: a default stronger than either the closed-world assumption or negation as failure, safe only when the arrangement makes the full search finish within the deadline | The medic's "If I can't find it, it isn't there" ([CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md)) and the owner's "if I can't find it quickly enough, it may as well not be there" ([CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md)) act on a failed search as if it showed absence. One find shows presence, but absence needs a check of everything, which a deadline forbids. First filed as negation as failure on a time bound, with Reiter and Clark unread. Both readings corrected it. The two assumptions are separate. Reiter's closed-world assumption is that the database is complete about the world. Clark's negation as failure is licensed only by finite failure: "the exhaustive but unsuccessful search for a proof". A search cut off by a deadline meets neither, so the rule is stronger than both. It assumes a closed world and that the unsearched part would have failed. It is safe when the full pass finishes in time. In [CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md) the EMT knew the drug was stocked, which is exactly where Reiter shows the closed-world assumption inconsistent. So there it was a decision to stop, not an inference. | Superseded — by [CLAIM-312](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-312.md) |
| [CLAIM-307](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-307.md) | Retrieval pressure and evidence are different criteria for carving a category, and they move in opposite directions with copy count: evidence that a distinction exists grows with its copies, the search a bin saves shrinks with them, so the bins a deadline forces are often the ones the data least supports | From [MOM-CLM-166](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-166.md), which reads the owner's LEGO parable ([CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md)) against a formalism that cited it with the sign reversed. [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md) says when a distinction is real enough to name. Its evidence grows with the number of copies. The parable says when a distinction must be built to act in time: a single brick among similar ones. Expected search falls as copies grow. The two answer different questions, "is it there?" and "can it be reached in time?", and come apart in both directions. MOM's table was re-run here and reproduced, and a simulation of the search agrees. | Active |
| [CLAIM-309](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-309.md) | How good a mixture is and how discriminable it is from its diluent come apart: under linear mixing a smoothie's distance from milk only shrinks as milk is added, so a preference that rises and then falls with milk is over the ratio and cannot be a d′, and the signal-detection reading of the owner's smoothie line reverses one of its directions | The smoothie note in the owner's LEGO monograph reads the owner's line ([CASE-096](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-096.md)) as signal detection. Milk is the noise, "Less Good" is d′ falling as the mixture approaches milk, and "More Good" is d′ rising as a little milk is added. Under linear mixing the mixture's taste is (1 − f)s + f·m, and its distance from milk is (1 − f)\|s − m\|. That falls monotonically from the first drop, so discriminability from milk cannot rise and then fall. The note's own first model is right: goodness is a single-peaked function of the ratio, which is a preference, not a discriminability. [MOM-CLM-166](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-166.md) found the same kind of reversal in the formal reading of the LEGO parable. MOM's record never mentions the smoothie note. | Active |
| [CLAIM-310](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md) v2 | Sorting schemes over objects with determinate properties never conflict as descriptions, since the product of any sortings refines them all; they conflict as arrangements, since a fixed number of bins realizes one partition when each item is stored once, and which costs least depends on what is searched for and on what stands out within a bin | What is directionally right in the owner's LEGO monograph, as Mathematics of Meaning graded it. Its contextuality claim is empty: any sortings of bricks share a joint refinement ([MOM-CLM-137](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-137.md)), and the events they generate stay Boolean ([MOM-ARG-047](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/arguments.d/ARG-047.md)). Its intuition that builders cannot share a sorting is true of arrangements. One set of bins realizes one partition, the product may need more bins than there are, and the cheapest choice depends on what each builder searches for and on what stands out within a bin ([CASE-095](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-095.md)). The disagreement is a trade, not a failure of global truth. Sorting on one attribute also turns a search for a combination of features into a search for one feature within each bin, which Treisman and Gelade (LIT-1082, read) show is the difference between a serial scan and one found at a glance. | Active |
| [CLAIM-312](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-312.md) v2 | "If I can't find it, it isn't there" asserts operational unavailability, that the item will not be put to use before the deadline, not absence: a search that fails by the deadline establishes unavailability outright, and licenses absence only with a certificate that the unsearched remainder cannot hold the item, from exhaustion, from an invariant of the arrangement, or from a closed-world default | Restates [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md) at the owner's request, after [CLAIM-311](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-311.md) showed that absence can be established without exhausting a collection. The owner's own wording in [CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md), "it may as well not be there", is hyperbole for operational availability ([TERM-055](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-055.md)), not a claim about inventory. Read so, the rule reports an outcome and needs no default. [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s analysis survives as the account of the literal reading: what a failed search must be joined with before it licenses absence. The gap between the two readings is [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s Bayes term, and it matters when the statement is passed to someone who will act on presence. | Active |
| [CLAIM-315](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-315.md) | In comparative anchoring tasks, considering an anchor shifts the later numerical estimate without adding evidence about the target, and the shift is carried by anchor-consistent knowledge made more accessible; the shift is established, the accessibility step is inferred and has not been measured | The empirical half of [CLAIM-298](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-298.md), split off under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md)'s pilot, which found that claim compound: an empirical claim about judgement tasks and an interpretive extension to communication in general. [CLAIM-298](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-298.md) now rests on it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-316](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-316.md) | A person's drive profile is time-indexed: who drives changes with state, such as hungry or sated and stressed or calm, with task and with regime | Split from [CLAIM-166](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-166.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the first of the owner's two parts of 2026-10-11, "'who drives' isn't a constant", stated on its own. It is argued from the drive-profile term and the will line's account of which regime is effective, and no observation the record holds estimates a person's drive profile over successive windows, so it is interpretive. The microbiome part, which the reviews support, stays in [CLAIM-166](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-166.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-317](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-317.md) v2 | Self-presentations that differ by audience do no harm while the audiences are kept apart; people keep them apart and script the occasions where they must meet, and broadcast and networked media bring them together unchosen, which is when the presentations collide | Split from [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the empirical half of that claim, the sociology of audiences on which its sheaf reading rests. Its evidence is boyd (2008, read in part in [NOTE-710](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-710.md)), after Meyrowitz (1985), and one documented collapse, [CASE-064](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-064.md). boyd's claims about collapse are documented with interviews and examples, not measured, and the Carmichael case reaches the record secondhand, so it stays Proposed. It says nothing about overlaps, covers or gluing; that is [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md)'s. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-318](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-318.md) | Within a shared observational scenario, exact structure-preserving symmetries are the invertible members of a nested family of stochastic transports, and among Markov kernels between finite sets the invertible ones are the permutation matrices, so the invertible core is the relabellings, a groupoid in which objects joined by an arrow have isomorphic automorphism groups | Split from [CLAIM-103](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-103.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the nesting and its invertible core, stated on their own so that their warrant can be. A110 §25 nests exact symmetries inside structure-compatible transports inside stochastic communicative transports, within a shared scenario, and the exact symmetries are the invertible ones. For Markov kernels between finite sets, a stochastic matrix with a stochastic inverse is a permutation matrix, because a nonnegative matrix with a nonnegative inverse is monomial, so the invertible core is the relabellings. In that groupoid an invertible u : A → B gives Aut(A) ≅ Aut(B), which corrects A198 §8. It does not say what symmetries are for: that they supply the yardstick for non-symmetric transports is [CLAIM-103](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-103.md)'s, and interpretive. | Active |
| [CLAIM-319](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-319.md) | Over a scenario of n contexts in an odd cycle, changing the support of one context takes the contextual fraction from 1 to 0 while the other n − 1 contexts and every marginal are kept exactly, at a weighted observational distortion of 1/n, so within a scenario the fraction's Lipschitz constant against that distortion is at least n; and any change of global extension needs a contextual model on one side | Split from [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the derivation that claim called "decisive and checkable", stated on its own. For odd n, an n-cycle of ±1 observables in which every context anticorrelates is strongly contextual; making one context correlate gives a model with a global distribution. The two agree on n − 1 contexts and on every marginal, differ by total variation 1 in the last, and so lie at weighted D_obs = 1/n with contextual fractions 1 and 0. For n = 3 it is [CASE-037](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-037.md) with one observable relabelled. It answers how small the local change can be; it says nothing about whether any data are contextual. | Active |
| [CLAIM-320](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-320.md) | Within one fixed measurement scenario, two no-signalling empirical models can agree on all but one of their contexts and on every single-observable marginal while their contextual fractions are 1 and 0, so keeping most local judgement distributions does not fix their global compatibility | Split from [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the possibility that claim's headline needs, shown by the pair it lost and recovered in [CASE-037](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-037.md). On the cover {AB, BC, AC} with binary outcomes, the parity triangle at 1/2 per allowed outcome is no-signalling and strongly contextual, with contextual fraction 1. Change only S_AC to {(0,0), (1,1)}: two contexts and every marginal are unchanged, and the model now extends to a global distribution, with fraction 0. It is an existence result by construction, and the weights are stipulated. It does not say reconstruction chains do this, which is [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md)'s thesis and interpretive, and the context that changes moves by a total-variation distance of 1. | Active |
| [CLAIM-321](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-321.md) v2 | In text-to-image diffusion models each condition of a prompt can be met while their conjunction or relational binding fails: benchmarks find single objects rendered almost always and attribute binding and relations failing most, and composing by adding scores does worst on relations | Split from [CLAIM-123](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-123.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the empirical part of that claim, that each condition can be met while their conjunction or relational binding fails, documented by GenEval, T2I-CompBench and T2I-CompBench++, by Attend-and-Excite's "catastrophic neglect", and by Composable Diffusion losing to an energy-based baseline on relations. It corroborates [CLAIM-123](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-123.md)'s derivation without carrying it, and does not say what causes the failures. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-322](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-322.md) v2 | Agreement under a probe family is evidence that two objects share structure only to the degree that the family was chosen independently of the comparison and is evaluated on cases it was not chosen on, so a family selected to make two objects look alike shows only that it can be selected | Split from [CLAIM-264](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-264.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): its evidential half, stated on its own so that its warrant can be. [CLAIM-264](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-264.md)'s exact half shows that agreement on a restricted probe family does not fix identity; this claim draws the rule for reading such agreement as evidence. It is an argument, not a theorem, so it is interpretive. It does not say which probes to choose, or that held-out probes are neutral. | Active |
| [CLAIM-323](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-323.md) v2 | Where source and rendering are experiments about one common situation, a rendering that depends on the situation other than through the source is not a garbling of it and can be incomparable with it in Blackwell's order: with Z uniform on {1, 2, 3}, a source that tells whether Z = 1 and a rendering that tells whether Z = 3 each have the lower 0–1 risk on one of the problems of saying whether Z = 1 and whether Z = 3, so neither dominates | Split from [CLAIM-258](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-258.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the worked case that objection uses, stated on its own so that its warrant can be. Over a common situation Z uniform on three values, U reports whether Z = 1 and V whether Z = 3. V is not a garbling of U, since given U = 0 it still varies with Z, and the risks on "say whether Z = 3" (0 from V, 1/3 from U) and "say whether Z = 1" (the reverse) show neither experiment dominates. It is an existence result by construction. It does not say this is the normal translation case, which is [CLAIM-258](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-258.md)'s reading and is interpretive. | Active |
| [CLAIM-324](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-324.md) v2 | In the What Survives Translation? exchange, the manuscript drafted straight from the crystallized argument changed the thesis with no turn arguing the move and dropped 24 of that argument's items, none on request, and the second crystallized argument announced its change of question but left items out without saying which had dissolved and which were lost | Split from [CLAIM-178](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-178.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the documented case on which that claim's normative conclusion rests, scoped to the one exchange it comes from. The evidence is the workbench reconstructions of that exchange (2026/10/09/025539, 2026/10/10/040457). One exchange, reconstructed turn by turn by the record's own readers; it says nothing about drafts in general. | Active |
| [CLAIM-325](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-325.md) | The behavioural data the record has read show no contextuality proper: none of the five kinds of data Dzhafarov, Zhang and Kujala re-analyse is contextual, Wang et al. test none of their 90 language systems for it, and no documented test of pragmatic or meaning judgements finds it at adequate power | Split from [CLAIM-219](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-219.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the empirical premise of that objection's dilemma, which [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md) conceded. Dzhafarov, Zhang and Kujala ([LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md), read in [NOTE-235](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-235.md)) find none of five kinds of behavioural data contextual, two of them previously published as contextual; Wang, Sadrzadeh, Abramsky and Cervantes ([LIT-851](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-851.md)) report signalling in 69 of 90 language systems and test none for contextuality; [CASE-053](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-053.md) collects the documented tests on elicited judgements and finds no contextual pragmatic data. It is scoped: [CASE-053](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-053.md) records a reliable positive result on instructed matching, so "none in behavioural data" is too broad, and the absence is [LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md)'s working hypothesis, not a proof that such data cannot exist. | Active |
| [CLAIM-326](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-326.md) v5 | With losses in [0, 1] and a stated prior, the positive part of the Bayes-risk increase on the same decision problem, D⁺_Q(U → V; π), is directed, is zero from a garbling back to its source, vanishes for every finite problem and prior exactly when the rendering is at least as informative as the source in Blackwell's order, over finitely many states and a source whose outcome space is standard Borel, and has A86's D_Q, with the identity on tasks, as its symmetrization | Split from [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the properties of the restated decision term, which [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md) called "elementary and checkable", stated on their own so that their warrant can be. Define D⁺_Q(U → V; π) = sup over q in Q of [r_q,π(V) − r_q,π(U)]⁺. A garbling never gains; with Q all finite problems and π all priors, the term vanishes exactly when V is at least as informative as U, by the Bayes form of Blackwell's theorem for finitely many states ([THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md)); it is directed; and A86's D_Q is its symmetrization. It does not say this is the right decision term, which is [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md)'s proposal, and it does not state the prior-free relation to Le Cam's deficiency. | Active |
| [CLAIM-327](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md) | A slowly changing collective variable, such as a reputation, a rivalry or a standing, is part of a collective's dynamics and not only an observer's average when its members read it, condition what they do on it, and by doing so regenerate it | A9 §3 and §10 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, after Flack 2012 (LIT-1122, unread). Three stages: an observer finds a stable statistic of fast interactions; members recognize it and use it; their use preserves or regenerates it. Only the third makes the variable an endogenous level. It is the general form of [CLAIM-277](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-277.md), where trust is the temporal regularity of endorsement that then steers endorsement. It does not say that such a variable individuates one collective: five slow variables sharing a referent may be five processes. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-328](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-328.md) v3 | When the continuities that ordinarily come bundled in a collective (legal franchise, civic role, interpersonal transmission, narrative and place) are separated, several later collectives can each be a genuine successor of the earlier one in a different respect, without any of them, or the earlier collective, having branched in numerical identity | A4's H5 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, in its weak form, on the Washington Senators. The league's successor to the original club is the Twins; the city's is the expansion Senators; the city's present team claims its history through place and narrative. Promoted from a section of [QUESTION-118](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-118.md) at the owner's word. It concerns plural successor relations, not branching identity, and rests on one documented case with no data on how supporters divided. | Active |
| [CLAIM-329](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-329.md) v5 | A collective that replaces all its members persists, when it does, by causal transmission of the organization that produces it, not by resemblance: an organization of the same kind that arises independently is not its continuation, and a lapse in its coherence need not end it | A5, A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-16. A9 §9 separated three persistences that dissociate: state persistence (a variable changes slowly), dynamical persistence (characteristic responses continue) and historical persistence (the producing processes are transmitted and reconstituted across successive populations). A5: "a system's ability to reproduce itself as the same kind is not automatically sufficient for its numerical persistence as the same individual." The second time the record meets "causal-organizational continuity": [CLAIM-280](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-280.md) noted A10 §4.3's of 2026-10-13 and did not file it. It does not say what must be transmitted, or settle branching successors. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md) | In the coupled meaning–influence model linearized at its symmetric state, with each field stable alone and nonnegative couplings, the coupling destabilizes symmetry exactly when βγ > (1 − α)(1 − δ): only the loop can do it, and the direction that grows mixes meaning and authority | A14 §2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, checked. For J = [[α, β], [γ, δ]] with nonnegative entries and α, δ < 1, the leading eigenvalue exceeds 1 iff βγ > (1 − α)(1 − δ). If either coupling is zero the eigenvalues are α and δ. The leading eigenvector is (β, λ+ − α), positive in both components. A partial answer to [QUESTION-100](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-100.md)'s "when the symmetric state is unstable", for the linearization only; it says nothing about the nonlinear attractors or about fidelity. | Active |
| [CLAIM-331](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md) v9 | A level of organization has a temporal facet as well as a compositional one: higher-level variables are characteristically slower and longer-lived than the activity that produces them, though slowness is a mark of a level and not its definition | The owner's, U8 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: "'higher level' doesn't just mean in terms of abstractions over abstractions, we should also expect 'higher level' effects to be on slower timescales than 'lower level' effects." A8 took it and qualified it: a market can crash and a stadium can chant in seconds, so timescale is "a facet of organizational level, not ... an ordering that must hold in every case". Simon's near-decomposability already ties weak coupling between blocks to slow aggregate dynamics ([LIT-905](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-905.md)). The claim does not say that a slow variable is thereby a level, a system or an individual. | Active |
| [CLAIM-332](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-332.md) v2 | A loosely organized population can change what an outside institution does through its members' separately motivated acts of making, selecting and passing things on, without forming a collective intention or judgment, when the organized pattern of those acts, and not only the acts of identifiable individuals, earns its place in explaining the change | A7's "distributed cultural uptake", of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on the owner's Juggernaut case. On A7's ladder (aggregate behaviour, amplification, collective causal efficacy, collective intention, corporate agency) it asserts the third rung and denies that the third needs the fourth. Promoted from a section of [QUESTION-119](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-119.md) at the owner's word, with A7's defeater priced by [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md), which A7 said it needed. It does not say the fandom was the efficacious unit. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-333](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-333.md) | Measuring every relevant variable is necessary but not sufficient for a Granger-causal analysis to say anything about interventions: the intervention must also be an isolated exogenous change and no influence may act within one sampling step, and then Granger noncausality implies no intervention effect and the effect is identified from the observational predictor, but a Granger-causal relation is still only potentially causal | The record's answer to [NOTE-010](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-010.md)'s C5, "if all relevant variables are measured, Granger- and Pearl-type analyses coincide", which the ΦID review asserts without conditions. Eichler and Didelez ([THEORY-704](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-704.md)) give sufficient conditions, and complete measurement is one of them. A two-variable process with nothing hidden shows it is not enough: a acts on b within one step, a is Granger-noncausal for b, and setting a(t) changes the mean of b(t + 1) by ργ. Checked by hand and by simulation. | Active |
| [CLAIM-335](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-335.md) v3 | Transfer entropy measures directed predictive improvement, not information flow: as a conditional mutual information it is the source's unique information about the target's next value plus its synergy with the target's past, so it can credit a source with a bit the source carries only jointly and read zero from sources that jointly fix the target, and conditioning on more series does not remove the synergy | The record's position on whether transfer entropy measures information flow. James, Barnett and Crutchfield show it does not, if flow is information attributable to the source alone ([THEORY-707](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-707.md)). Williams and Beer's decomposition shows why, for any partial information decomposition satisfying the consistency equations ([THEORY-712](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-712.md)). Both papers' examples were recomputed exactly. This is a different failure from [CLAIM-333](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-333.md)'s, prediction against intervention. It leaves transfer entropy standing as a predictive quantity. | Active |
| [CLAIM-336](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-336.md) v6 | The pragmatic-transport and will-organization lines describe one model, an organization of operators that act on a shared interpretive state under a context while allocating one another's influence: a frame is the context under which operators act, a judgement is the response they yield, an action-generating regime is an operator or coalition, and a will-organization is the dynamics that allocates influence among them | The owner's, U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: the pragmatic-transport model and the will-organization model are "both manifestations of the same underlying model". The mapping is the assistant's, A6, filed at the owner's request ("address the still open stuff"). At U8 the owner endorsed it as filed ("Yes, as filed"). It reads both lines into [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s operator model. The sharp edge: it says the lines share one model, not that either line's results transfer to the other unchanged. Each mapping is a hypothesis until a result on one line is shown to hold, through it, on the other. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-338](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-338.md) v2 | The selectivity active inference gives action, sampling what one expects to experience, is played in the coupled meaning–authority model by the authority space: influence decides which operators retrieve and so what the next judgement observes, which makes Friston's self-confirming sampling the model's authority-to-interpretation arrow and his agent a coupled loop run without independent scoring | The owner's, U10 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on Friston et al.'s "sampling selectively what one expects to experience": "I think this selectivity maps to the authority space in my coupled model." Worked out by A10. Selective sampling is the β arrow of [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md), authority shaping interpretation through what it retrieves. Policies scored on current beliefs are the γ arrow. So Friston's agent runs both arrows, and his "this weakness becomes the strength" accepts capture, with the anchor moved outside the loop to selection on whole agents. The sharp edge: the mapping relocates sampling from the world to retrieval, which is [CLAIM-337](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-337.md)'s move reversed, and it holds only if the agent's own store can surprise it as the world can. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-340](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-340.md) | Scoring operators on predictions committed before the evidence is not by itself Regime B: in the linearized operator model the coupling of interpretation to endorsement has the sign of κ′ − κ̄, so commitment removes capture only when the interpretation bends the reading of the evidence no more than it bends the predictions, and it keeps the learning that revising after the evidence would lose | The formal question [QUESTION-121](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-121.md) asked, answered in [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md)'s linearization ([CASE-106](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-106.md)): is committing predictions before the evidence equivalent to Regime B? No. The coupling γ is 4ηs(κ′ − κ̄), where κ̄ is how far the shared meaning bends the committed predictions and κ′ how far it bends the reading of the evidence. It is corrective, null or capturing as κ′ is below, at or above κ̄. Strong correction can fail by oscillation when \|βγ\| ≥ 1 − αδ. Revising predictions after the evidence sets γ = 0 but also stops authority from tracking who predicts well. Linear, at the symmetric state, for squared-error scoring. | Active |
| [CLAIM-341](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-341.md) v2 | The loop that keeps a lucid agent's model in touch with what it models runs between judgement and observation: each judgement reshapes the observer whose later observations it then judges, and action on the world is not part of that loop, so active inference's action–perception cycle misplaces where the agent is active | The owner's, U1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: Friston's free-energy approach is "generally correct, but the cybernetic model is wrong"; action can be cut out of the loop, which decomposes into "Judgement (qua measurement that generates interpretations) <--> Observation". At U2 the owner held that the pragmatic-transport and will-organization models are "both manifestations of the same underlying model". The claim is stated in that model's terms, as [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s circuit, and in the diachronic form A4 proposed and the owner asked to be filed at U5 ("make the revisions"): a judgement need not produce the observation it judges, but it reshapes the observer that produces the next one. The sharp edge: the synchronic form, in which each judgement produces its own outcome, is not claimed. That is the open route of [TERM-039](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-039.md) and [CLAIM-127](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-127.md), and the record demoted it once before ([CLAIM-109](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-109.md)). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md) v3 | What keeps a judgement–observation loop from confirming itself is evidence whose arrival or scoring does not pass through the interpretation it tests; action is one source of such evidence, not a necessary one, and a loop that selects its own evidence can lock in with action available | The assistant's synthesis, A3 and A4 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, filed at the owner's request at U5. Three results the record already holds. [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md): capture in the operator model needs both arrows of [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s circuit, and scoring operators independently of the dominant interpretation removes it. [CLAIM-141](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-141.md): a loop always has a distributional fixed point, so what binds it is a constraint that prescribes marginals. [THEORY-285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md) ([NOTE-766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-766.md)): an active-inference agent locks in with action available, because its own sampling policy withholds the evidence that would correct it. The claim does not say action is unimportant, only that it is not what does the anchoring. | Active |
| [CLAIM-343](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-343.md) | For three or more parts, no ΦID can use a redundancy function that both satisfies the identity axiom and yields nonnegative atoms, because on the Williams–Beer lattice the two are inconsistent from three sources up; a ΦID verdict on three or more parts therefore rests on which axiom the analyst drops, and should name it | The record's answer to the gap left by the PID filing: no held measure gave ΦID an identity-respecting redundancy for more than two sources. Rauh et al. show none can, on the lattice ΦID uses, without a negative atom ([THEORY-713](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-713.md)). The record's measures split the difference: I_min keeps atoms nonnegative by calling independent copied bits redundant, and Ince's I_ccs keeps an independent-sources identity and reports a −1-bit atom ([THEORY-714](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-714.md)). Two-part ΦID is untouched. | Active |
| [CLAIM-344](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-344.md) v3 | Resolve is a maintained organization of precedence, commitment and revision that keeps a temporally extended policy effective across changes in locally dominant evaluations while keeping the capacity to revise it; mere slowness or persistence is not resolve | The owner's frame, U37 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "I think emergence of "resolve" could be an interesting frame within which to examine our will-organization framework." A37 defined it, and A39 to A47 revised it each turn: retention and revision as separate grades, fragility against rigidity (A41), access against authority (A42), and governance that makes its own repeated exercise unnecessary (A45, A47). The record already holds a theory of resolve, Ainslie's recursive staking of future choices ([THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md)); this is its organizational and revisable form, placed in [CLAIM-159](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-159.md)'s will-organization cell. The sharp edge: the standard for when revision is warranted is not supplied, and is [QUESTION-087](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-087.md)'s open problem. | Active |
| [CLAIM-345](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-345.md) | Equal controllability rank does not fix the cost of control: for x_{t+1} = x_t + b·u the least quadratic effort for a displacement Δ is Δ²/b², unbounded as b → 0 while the system stays controllable, and in general the least effort is Δxᵀ W_T^† Δx, set by the Gramian and not by its rank | A9 §2 and A12's Proposition 1 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, the step the owner's U9 "controllability of a system isn't binary" needs. For a scalar step x_{t+1} = x_t + b·u the cheapest input costs Δ²/b², so two systems that are both controllable can differ in cost by any factor. The general statement is the minimum-energy formula with the controllability Gramian. A9: "This is already a standard result from linear control theory." Proved here because the record holds no source for it. The sharp edge: the cost is relative to a fixed input norm, and rescaling the input makes every b cost the same, so comparing costs across systems needs inputs in common units. | Active |
| [CLAIM-346](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-346.md) | Feasibility, aggregation and epistemic coordination are independent obstructions to an organization's realizing its demands: each can occur with the other two absent | Owner-seeded, U36 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: Arrow's theorem, then cryptography and "the two generals problem". A36 placed them: "Arrow's theorem belongs in the theory of endorsement, not directly in the geometry of feasible updates", and the two generals add "epistemic frustration". Three elementary constructions, each with one obstruction and not the others, are given in the body. The sharp edge: the independence is relative to fixing the demands as the constituents' own acceptance conditions; that no remedy for one removes another is A36's further reading, argued in the body and not part of the claim. | Active |
| [CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md) v3 | Frustration among an organization's demands is an ordinal fact before it is a quantity: the jointly satisfiable sets of demands form a downward-closed complex whose minimal non-faces are the minimal conflicts, relief is strict enlargement of that complex for the same declared demands, reorganizations that relieve different conflicts are incomparable, and dropping or suppressing a demand is not relief | The owner's correction, U37 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "We can do quite a lot with access to an ordering, even if it doesn't give us a true measure." A37 granted it ("I agree with your correction") and built the acceptance sets, their intersection and the compatibility complex. Corrected here: acceptance conditions sit on attainable outcomes, a demand's form depends on whether it demands improvement or maintenance, and A37's weak-preference sets fail only as representations of improvement demands. The definitional facts are shown in the body, including that every pair of demands can be jointly improvable while the triple is not. The sharp edge: relief compares complexes for the same declared demands, so a reorganization that deletes a demand is not compared at all, and two reorganizations can be incomparable. It is the move [CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md) and [TERM-043](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md) made for translation, in a new line. | Active |
| [CLAIM-348](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md) v4 | No coarse-graining is normatively adequate in general because it preserves stability, prediction or aggregate performance: a description adequate for an institution's performance can merge states its members' claims must distinguish, so adequacy is fixed by the evaluative target, and the target cannot be justified solely by the description that preserves it | A21 §18's Candidate 2 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, with A21 §5's clause against circularity and A22's Construction C ([CASE-110](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-110.md)). | [CLAIM-349](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-349.md) v5 | An organization's access to a signal, the signal's authority over action, and action on it are separable, and adaptive regulation keeps the first while making the second conditional on evidence; overcontrol, which buys freedom from harmful acts by cutting access or making inhibition unconditional, is a maladaptive regime and not more control, so flexibility is a context-sensitive property of maintained influence relations, not of how much is inhibited | The owner's idea, U42 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A41's line that an organization "could become extremely resistant to internal changes while losing its capacity to learn, correct errors, or act at all": "useful connections to the ACT and DBT frameworks here, which provide us with accounts/ontologies of maladaption and productive flexibility". | [CLAIM-351](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-351.md) | A zero aggregate gradient does not show that the demands it aggregates are reconciled: with positive weights it holds both when every demand's own gradient vanishes and when nonzero gradients cancel, and in the second case no update improves them all to first order; even the first is only joint first-order stationarity, which a demand's maximum or saddle also has | A33 §5 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "Zero aggregate gradient does not imply absence of frustrated demands." | [CLAIM-352](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-352.md) v2 | Sen's two aspects of freedom divide along the record's line between what an agent can viably reach and the organization that selects among it: viable reachability can stand for the opportunity aspect only through a map from trajectories to valued functionings, which control theory does not supply, and will-organization gives a causal account of part of the process aspect, not of its fairness or legitimacy | The owner's connection, U11 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, quoting A9 and A10 on viable reachability: "This feels reminiscent of ideas from moral philosophy, e.g. Amartya Sen capabilities account." | [CLAIM-353](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-353.md) | A will-organization that gives two operators decisive jurisdiction over a pair of options each, respects unanimous preference and admits any profile of operator rankings cannot always choose, and unlike Arrow's impossibility this is not escaped by giving endorsement richer, cardinal or comparable, information, so what distributed governance must give up is jurisdiction, unanimity or the domain, not an informational restriction | From U36 of the exchange of 2026-10-17. | [CLAIM-354](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-354.md) v2 | Freedom of will and autonomy come in degrees along several dimensions, among them viable reachability, control cost, robustness to disturbance, governance reconfigurability, revisability and motivational integration, and agents compare by inclusion of what they can viably reach under matched conditions: a partial order with incomparable pairs, not a scalar, and a gradient only of a declared measure | The owner's, U9 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "controllability of a system isn't binary, and neither is sensitivity to perturbation", so can the account speak of "gradations (perhaps even gradients/spectra?) of freedom of will/autonomy". | [CLAIM-355](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-355.md) v4 | In a distributed agent the binding of appraisal, readiness and governance into one response can be real while the single owner a self-model or collective self-description attributes it to is a representational construction, not a further entity; the illusion, where there is one, is in the attribution and belongs to whichever system adopts the representation, and this deflates the self without settling whether experience is real | The owner's, U26 and U27 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: at U26 whether, "adopting an illusionist/fictionalist position", the record can make claims about subjecthood; at U27, "illusory binding-type phenomena in distributed agents", starting from the record's emotion material. | [CLAIM-356](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-356.md) v2 | An objective that originates outside a learning system can become a goal of the training organization, through its causal role in selecting, stabilizing and reproducing the learned structure it rewards; exogenous origin does not disqualify a goal, but it does not show that the network governs or endorses the objective, and what is selected is performance on the updating distribution, not generalization | The owner's, U35 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, against A34's guardrail that "Loss minimization does not automatically mean the model has its own goals": the externally assigned objective "can motivate identification and persistence of learned features", so the training process can be described as "having endogenous goals". | [CLAIM-357](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-357.md) v4 | The frustration residual and governance regret separate structural infeasibility, realized violation and minimax suboptimality, and identify none of them as thwarting: a positive residual says no admissible update meets every declared requirement, a positive regret only that the actual update's worst residual exceeds the best achievable, which can hold while every requirement is met, and actual violation needs regret above the negative residual; aggregate performance does not tell infeasibility from realized violation, and the multipliers that certify infeasibility are not the weights governance assigns | A34 §4 and A35 §3.3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, restated at A39 §2C and A40 §3.4, from A33's "irreducible conflict" and "manufactured frustration". With m(d) the worst residual, Φ its minimum and Γ the actual update's excess over Φ ([CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md)): Φ > 0 is structural infeasibility; when Φ ≤ 0 the actual update violates a requirement exactly when Γ > −Φ. | [CLAIM-358](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-358.md) v2 | Learned local accommodation can reduce the amortized cost of recurrent arbitration: where a recurring conflict among an agent's processes admits a stable accommodation, settling it among the processes can cost less over repeated encounters than escalating each instance to a higher-level process that mediates or overrides, though local negotiation and the relations it needs are not free | The owner's, U45 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "processes which can navigate disagreement amongst themselves require fewer resources from the system than processes which need to activate additional subsystems to resolve disagreement." | [CLAIM-359](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-359.md) | A self-governing organization's robustness to compromised constituents is a property of the processes that allocate, audit and revise authority, not only of its constraints on harmful acts; safeguards against capture can also restrict the disagreement and revision that self-governance needs, and where they do security and self-governance trade off, while others, such as audits independent of the audited that protect dissent, serve both, so the two are distinct achievements and not opposed ones | The owner's question, U41 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "is literature on organizational robustness to insider threats potentially useful to us?" | [CLAIM-369](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-369.md) | In symmetric resource-mediated competition with interaction matrix A = UᵀU and growth rates r = Uᵀb − c, Lotka–Volterra population dynamics are multiplicative gradient flow on the convex feature-selection objective ½‖b − Un‖² + cᵀn over the nonnegative orthant: the invasion fitness of an absent component is the negative partial derivative of that objective, and the uninvadable equilibria are its KKT points | From a synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18 (workbench entry of that date), checked here and given a proof.
