| [CLAIM-377](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-377.md) | For any differentiable model under squared loss with Gaussian noise of precision β, the model's Fisher on n inputs is the Gauss–Newton matrix βJᵀJ, and its non-zero eigenvalues are exactly β times those of the empirical NTK Gram matrix JJᵀ, with the same multiplicities, its eigenvectors being Jᵀ applied to the Gram matrix's, normalized | [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md)'s Step 1, stated as the record's own and proved. Through the SVD J = UΣVᵀ, JᵀJ and JJᵀ share the non-zero eigenvalues σ_i² with equal multiplicities, and Jᵀu/σ is the eigenvector of JᵀJ for a unit eigenvector u of JJᵀ. Under y \| x ~ N(f(x; θ), β⁻¹), the expected outer product of the score is β∇f∇fᵀ, which summed over inputs is βJᵀJ, the Gauss–Newton matrix. "Fisher" means the model's Fisher, not the empirical Fisher of observed residuals. It holds at every width, in every regime and on any data. It says nothing about what the spectrum looks like, which is [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md)'s. | Active |
| [CLAIM-378](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-378.md) | A representational similarity index invariant to every invertible linear map depends on a representation only through its column space, so it takes one value on all column-centred representations of rank n − 1, as it does on all representations of rank n | The generalization of [THEORY-236](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-236.md)'s theorem. If col(X) = col(Y), write X = BC and Y = BD with B a basis of the common column space and C, D of full row rank, extend C and D to invertible matrices, and the quotient maps X onto Y. Since XA always has the column space of X, the GL(p) orbits are exactly the sets of n × p matrices sharing a column space. Theorem 1 is the case of column space ℝⁿ. Column-centred matrices of rank n − 1 all have column space 1^⊥, so an invariant index cannot tell them apart either. | Active |
| [CLAIM-379](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-379.md) | On a finite set of stimuli, regularized linear readouts with ridge b > 0 cannot tell apart two centred representations of the same width exactly when one is an orthogonal transformation of the other, and the unregularized CCA member cannot tell apart representations with the same column space, which differ by an invertible linear map | The proved core of [CLAIM-269](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-269.md). What a regularized linear readout decodes is a function of K_X = X G⁻¹ Xᵀ/M, with G = aC_X + bI ([THEORY-008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md)). For b > 0, K_X and the Gram matrix XXᵀ determine each other, by a monotone map on the shared eigenvalues; and equal Gram matrices mean an orthogonal transformation ([CLAIM-290](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-290.md), [THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md)). For b = 0, K_X is the projection onto the column space, which fixes X only up to an invertible linear map, as for a softmax layer ([THEORY-723](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-723.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-380](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-380.md) v2 | With finitely many states and finitely many outcomes, the positive part of the Bayes-risk increase on the same decision problem is directed, is zero from a garbling back to its source, vanishes for every finite problem and prior exactly when the rendering is at least as informative as the source, and has A86's D_Q as its symmetrization | The finite-outcome part of [CLAIM-326](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-326.md). Define D⁺_Q(U → V; π) = sup over q in Q of [r_q,π(V) − r_q,π(U)]⁺, with losses in [0, 1] and a stated prior. A garbling never gains. The term is directed. A86's D_Q is its symmetrization. And with every finite problem and prior, it vanishes exactly when V is at least as informative as U, by Blackwell's Theorem 6 ([THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md)). It does not cover outcome spaces that are not finite, or say this is the right decision term. | Active |
| [CLAIM-381](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-381.md) | Over a finite class of items with finite judgement outcomes, a constant outcome kernel fits every item only when the target readers' averaged responses do not vary with the item, an exact fit is a garbling with the item as common parameter, and Le Cam's deficiency and its restriction to finitely many decision problems are finite computations | The derivational core of [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md). Over a finite class of items, the target term is the readers' response averaged over a procedure's output, and one outcome kernel family is fixed across the items. Then a constant kernel fits only target responses that carry no information about the item. An exact fit is a garbling, with the item as the common parameter. And Le Cam's deficiency between the two finite tables is one linear programme. Its restriction to finitely many decision problems is a finite computation. It does not say the measure is informative, which is [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md)'s empirical question. | Active |
| [CLAIM-382](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-382.md) | In an autoencoder initialised with i.i.d. Gaussian weights and zero biases and trained by SGD or momentum SGD on a loss of its output, the law of each hidden layer's learned representation is invariant under every orthogonal map of that layer that commutes with its activation, so under a radial activation no basis is privileged in law, while elementwise tanh or Leaky-ReLU yields invariance only under the signed permutations or the permutations, which leaves the standard axes free to be privileged | [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md)'s symmetry argument, stated as the record's own and proved. Transform the parameters by orthogonal maps Q_l of the hidden spaces that commute with the activation. The network then computes Q_l h_l and the same output, so the loss is invariant. Gradient steps commute with the transformation, and an i.i.d. Gaussian initialisation is invariant under it, so the law of the trained representations is too. For radial activations this is all of O(n), and no basis is privileged in law. For elementwise ones it is a finite group, so the axes may be privileged. Whether they are, and how strongly, is [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md)'s empirical content. The argument needs an orthogonally equivariant optimiser, and fails for Adam. | Active |
| [CLAIM-383](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-383.md) | In plane Couette and plane Poiseuille flow, measured in the energy norm, the linearized operator about the laminar profile has transient growth at least cR and resolvent norm at least cR² with c independent of R, so wherever it is eigenvalue-stable a perturbation of norm at most CR⁻² makes it eigenvalue-unstable | [THEORY-304](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-304.md)'s scalings as lower bounds, derived. At streamwise wavenumber zero, the cross-stream velocities obey an R-independent Stokes problem in the time t/R. They force the streamwise velocity through −U′v, so the streamwise response is R times an R-independent field. In the energy norm this gives transient growth at least cR, and in the steady forced problem a resolvent norm at least cR². Through pseudospectra, a perturbation of norm O(R⁻²) then moves an eigenvalue into the unstable half-plane wherever the flow is eigenvalue-stable. The sharp constants, and that the growth is no more than order R, come from the computation and are not here. | Active |
| [CLAIM-384](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-384.md) | For a network linearised at its initial parameters, with an isotropic Gaussian prior of precision α on the parameter displacement and Gaussian noise of precision β, the log-determinant part of the evidence is −½ Σ log(1 + βλ/α) over the non-zero eigenvalues λ of the empirical neural tangent kernel's Gram matrix on the training inputs, so at most n directions are priced however many parameters the network has |  | Active |
| [CLAIM-385](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-385.md) v2 | If a symmetric operator on ℝⁿ commutes with an orthogonal representation of a compact group, each eigenspace is a sum of real irreducibles and each multiplicity a sum of multiples of their dimensions, so SO(2) and ℤ/n for n ≥ 3 force paired eigenvalues; conversely the spectrum fixes neither the group nor a basis inside an eigenspace |  | Active |
| [CLAIM-386](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-386.md) | For x(t+1) = (A* + εC)x with A* block-diagonal, the Simon–Ando aggregate Â = QAV has one-step closure defect exactly QA − ÂQ = QA(I − VQ); the part from the blocks' own dynamics vanishes iff every block has equal column sums, and then the whole defect is ε·QC(I − VQ) | Derived in the reading of Shpak, Stadler, Wagner and Altenberg (2004), [NOTE-977](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-977.md), which states the Simon–Ando aggregate without an error term, and re-checked here. It splits the closure defect of block aggregates into a part from coupling between blocks, which is exactly first order in ε, and a part from the blocks' own dynamics, which vanishes exactly in the equitable case of [THEORY-755](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-755.md). Deterministic dynamics, one step; the post-transient orders reported below are numerical, not part of the claim. | Active |
| [CLAIM-387](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-387.md) | Optimal deterministic information-bottleneck partitions at two budgets need not be nested: with X uniform on four states and binary Y with P(Y=1\|x) = (0, 0, 1/8, 3/8), the optimum is {0,1,2 \| 3} for 6.91 < β < 9.26 and {0,1 \| 2,3} for 9.26 < β < 16.06, two partitions neither of which refines the other | Found by brute force in the reading of Equitz and Cover ([NOTE-988](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-988.md)) and re-run here from scratch. It answers the deterministic half of [QUESTION-220](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-220.md) in the negative: raising the budget can reorganize the optimal partition rather than split it. The two optima are not even laminar, so no fixed tree holds both as prunings, and [NOTE-676](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-676.md)'s nesting is bought by its tree restriction. It says nothing about stochastic encoders, where finite-β optima generally live ([THEORY-743](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-743.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-388](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-388.md) v3 | Exact dynamical closure of a collective variable does not require a nearly decomposable block: in a linear Gaussian VAR(1) with uniform coupling among n units, the sum of all units is exactly dynamically independent at every stable coupling strength, while every partition of the units into two or more groups couples as strongly across its edges as within them | From A5 of the exchange of 2026-10-19 on coarse-to-fine processes, which gave the two-unit continuous-time case (ż = (b − a)z for z = x₁ + x₂) and the boxed slogan "Exact aggregation ⇏ near-decomposability". Made exact here for n units with [THEORY-733](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-733.md)'s sufficiency condition, and checked numerically. It answers the converse half of [QUESTION-221](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-221.md). It does not say the closed sum is one system ([QUESTION-218](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-218.md)), and it is about partitions of the units: in the eigenbasis of A the same system is exactly decomposable, which is the point. | Active |
| [CLAIM-389](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-389.md) v2 | In a stable linear Gaussian VAR(1), exact dynamical independence of a linear coarse-graining implies that its Mori–Zwanzig memory vanishes, but not conversely: memory needs coupling out of the coarse variable and back, and dependence needs only the way back, so a coarse variable can be Markov in its own law with zero memory and still be dynamically dependent | Derived in the reading of Chorin, Hald and Kupferman (2000), [NOTE-989](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-989.md), and re-checked here. It settles, for the linear Gaussian VAR(1) class, the relation [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md) left open between memory in the reduced dynamics and [THEORY-257](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-257.md)'s dynamical independence: memory is the round trip Y → rest → Y, dependence the inward leg alone. Not about VAR(p ≥ 2), where the reading reports that an independent variable can carry memory, nor about nonlinear systems. | Active |
| [CLAIM-390](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-390.md) | For a block of coordinates in a stable linear Gaussian VAR(1), dynamical dependence is at most ½ log det(I + Σ_YY⁻¹ A_YR C A_YRᵀ), with A_YR the coupling into the block and C the covariance of the rest given the block's present state, so it is of second order in the coupling into the block, whatever the coupling out of it | First found in the reading of Chorin, Hald and Kupferman (2000), [NOTE-989](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-989.md), as a by-product; derived and checked here. It answers the forward half of [QUESTION-221](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-221.md) for a block's full state: weak coupling into a block makes its dynamical dependence small, to second order. It is about the block's full state, not its aggregate. For the aggregate, the block's own internal dynamics add a defect of their own ([CLAIM-386](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-386.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-391](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-391.md) | For any classes with weights π_c and per-class factor matrices H_c and Δ_c, the class-wise Kronecker product Σ_c π_c H_c ⊗ Δ_c exceeds the product of the weighted averages H̄ ⊗ Δ̄ by exactly the weighted between-class covariance Σ_c π_c (H_c − H̄) ⊗ (Δ_c − Δ̄), so the two agree when either factor is the same in every class |  | Active |
| [CLAIM-392](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-392.md) v2 | Stochastic information-bottleneck optima at two budgets need not be nested: for X uniform on four states and binary Y with P(Y=1\|x) = (0, 0, 1/8, 3/8), the unique optima at β = 8 and β = 12 admit no Markov chain X → T₂ → T₁, so raising the budget reorganizes the optimum even with noisy encoders | Computed in the reading of Charvin, Catenacci Volpi and Polani (2023), [NOTE-981](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-981.md), on the source of [CLAIM-387](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-387.md), and re-run here. With [THEORY-753](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-753.md)'s criterion (refinable iff some pair of optima forms the chain, iff the coarse decoder points lie in the fine decoder hull when that hull is non-degenerate), and optima certified unique, the hull test fails. It answers the stochastic half of [QUESTION-220](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-220.md) in the negative for this source. The certificate is numerical, not interval arithmetic, and the loss is small: 0.49% of the larger budget, in unique information. | Active |
| [CLAIM-394](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-394.md) | In a stationary linear Gaussian VAR(1) that is time-reversible (AΠ = ΠAᵀ, Π the stationary covariance), every slow-feature direction is a left eigenvector of A, so any span of slow features is an exactly dynamically independent coarse-graining; off reversibility a slow feature is in general neither independent nor free of memory | Derived in the reading of Schüler and Wiskott (2025), [NOTE-1015](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1015.md), and re-checked here. It says when slowness, the criterion of slow feature analysis ([THEORY-746](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-746.md)), picks out a closed coarse-graining in [THEORY-733](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-733.md)'s sense: always in the reversible linear Gaussian VAR(1), which is the class of noise-free square mixtures of independent AR(1) processes, and not in general otherwise. Linear features, linear Gaussian dynamics, lag one. | Active |
| [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md) | Under Montévil and Mossio's definition of closure, a closed set of constraints has at least two members, and if each constraint is produced at the time scale of a constraint in the set that generates it and not at the scale at which it is itself conserved, the set includes at least one slow and one fast dependence, so a system with a single constraint of its own cannot realise closure |  | Active |
| [CLAIM-396](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-396.md) | Directional information measures between reciprocally coupled units follow the path of a one-sided drive rather than the symmetry of the coupling, so the observed direction of information flow does not by itself reveal which way, or whether both ways, the units are coupled | The record's generalization of one study (Das, Manikandan and Banerjee, [THEORY-275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-275.md)) beyond its system, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 as the record's own claim, since the source makes no general claim. It bears on the claims that read peer or hierarchical architecture from the direction of coupling. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-397](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-397.md) v2 | For a scalar stationary process with autocovariance C, the Mori–Zwanzig memory kernels for the projection onto the current value are fixed by C alone, through C(m+1) = Σ_{k≤m} c_k C(m−k); the memory vanishes iff C is geometric, and when C has finite Hankel rank d the memory has Hankel rank exactly d − 1 | Derived in the reading of Lin and Lu (2019), [NOTE-1029](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1029.md), and re-checked here. It settles the minimal-order question [CLAIM-398](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-398.md) left open, for every scalar stationary process with rational autocovariance, and gives the structural reason for [CLAIM-389](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-389.md)'s "not conversely": the memory is a functional of the coarse variable's own law, so it cannot register dependence on the rest of the system. | Active |
| [CLAIM-398](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-398.md) | In a stable linear Gaussian VAR(1) on ℝⁿ, a scalar linear coarse variable Y = LX is, in its own law, an ARMA process of orders at most (n, n − 1); so its Mori–Zwanzig memory, though non-zero at every lag in general, is carried exactly by finitely many coordinates that are functions of Y's own past and innovations | Derived in the reading of Chorin and Lu (2015), [NOTE-1028](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1028.md), and re-checked here. Their NARMAX closures are fitted, with no error bound; in the linear Gaussian class the same idea is exact. A coarse variable with memory admits a finite Markovian augmentation built only from its own history, which is the augmentation [THEORY-257](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-257.md)'s criterion conditions on. Scalar Y, VAR(1), Gaussian noise. | Active |
| [CLAIM-399](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-399.md) | Causal abstraction in the senses of Rubenstein et al., Beckers and Halpern, and Beckers, Eberhardt and Halpern does not secure governance-response sufficiency: exact transformation, τ-abstraction and zero approximate-abstraction distance all accept the hidden-bit coarse-graining, which loses ρ(h = 1) bits of the response to h, because each lets high-level noise carry what the coarse state drops; for one outcome and the identity correspondence, sufficiency is their compatibility condition with the high-level context fixed to the coarse state, and strong abstraction rejects the case only through interventions on the hidden parameter | The record's join, on 2026-10-21, of its readings of the causal-abstraction papers ([NOTE-1037](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1037.md), [NOTE-1032](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1032.md), [NOTE-1045](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1045.md)) with [CLAIM-407](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md). A25 of the exchange of 2026-10-20: "We should not present governance-preserving coarse-graining as a new general theory of causal abstraction." That stands. But it is not an instance of these papers' notions either: their criteria compare interventional laws and let the high-level context be any map that works, so they accept the hidden governance bit, whose coarse state keeps nothing of the response to h. Re-checked step by step against the three THEORYs. It corrects [TERM-067](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-067.md)'s first wording, which read the profile as [TERM-043](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md)'s causal component with the identity correspondence. | Active |
| [CLAIM-400](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-400.md) v3 | In the meaning–authority model linearized at symmetry, a third, maintained legibility state that authority moves (ε) and that moves interpretation (ν) or endorsement (μ), with persistence λ < 1 and nonnegative couplings, destabilizes the symmetric state exactly when the two-variable condition holds with β + νε/(1 − λ) in place of β and δ + με/(1 − λ) in place of δ: at the threshold the regime is indistinguishable from stronger two-variable couplings, and the slower it is the more it adds, while away from the threshold it adds a mode that no two-variable model has, so a lean in the regime can outlast the advantages it was built from | [QUESTION-253](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-253.md) asked whether authority's effect on what becomes legible as evidence is a third channel with its own instability condition, or [CLAIM-340](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-340.md)'s κ′ renamed. Both, in different respects. With a maintained legibility state r, det(I − J₃) = (1 − λ)[(1 − α)(1 − δ) − βγ] − ε[νγ + μ(1 − α)], which is (1 − λ) times [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md)'s expression with β_eff = β + νε/(1 − λ) and δ_eff = δ + με/(1 − λ). So the instability threshold is a two-variable one with stronger couplings, and a slower regime (λ near 1) adds more. Away from the threshold, r is a third mode: a lean in the regime can hold interpretation and authority off symmetry after they would have relaxed, which no two-variable parameters reproduce. | Active |
| [CLAIM-401](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-401.md) v3 | The conditions an effective description is commonly asked to meet are not of one kind: predictive sufficiency and approximation fidelity are adequacy relative to a declared target, metric and horizon; tractability restricts the operations under which adequacy is assessed; dynamical independence and memory closure are relations of the representation to the system, memory relative to a chosen projection; so a matrix over them as independent binary axes conflates kinds | A4 and A5 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U4 ("it sounds like considering it from this angle has potentially already altered our characterization of those 'virtues'"). A4: "(P) and (A) look increasingly like evaluation criteria, while (D) and (M) describe different aspects of system–representation structure. (C) describes resource accessibility." A5: approximation fidelity "may specify the degree to which a prediction or dynamical relation is preserved", and tractability "can instead restrict the operations over which preservation is evaluated". The record adds what A5 missed: memory is relative to the projection too ([QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md), [THEORY-752](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-752.md), [CLAIM-397](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-397.md)). It is [CLAIM-348](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md)'s "adequacy is fixed by the evaluative target" applied to the axes of a comparison. It does not say the five reduce to three. | Active |
| [CLAIM-402](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-402.md) v3 | Predictive success of a category across contexts warrants treating it as a real effective kind only when the evidence in those contexts does not pass through the category's own use, or when the effect of that use is modelled: a category that speakers or institutions act on can produce the regularities that confirm it, and contexts that share its use are not independent | A27 §1 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U27 ("are we perhaps better positioned now to address [QUESTION-007](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-007.md)? -009? -011? -028?"), after A26 §2's performative toy. It is the one criterion A27 added to A191's four on [QUESTION-028](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-028.md)'s page, and [NOTE-769](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-769.md) anticipated it from Hacking's interactive kinds. [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md)'s condition on evidence, moved from a judgement–observation loop to the warrant for a kind. The sharp edge: it defeats one inference and is not a criterion of kindhood, so [QUESTION-028](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-028.md) stays Open. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-403](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-403.md) v4 | A contribution's admission to an organization's inquiry, its recognition in apt terms, its credibility, its uptake into judgements, and its contributor's part in revising the standards of uptake are separable, each possible without the later ones, so an organization can widen access while every channel by which a less authoritative contribution could change the criteria of authority stays closed | A24 §6 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U24: "Someone's contribution may be received and politely acknowledged yet have no mechanism through which it can change institutional understanding." A25 §5 repeated the split from the side of visibility, and A27 §6 used it of consultation. [CLAIM-349](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-349.md) has the three-step form for an organization's own signals. This carries it to contributors and adds the top rung, Longino's tempered equality and [QUESTION-041](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-041.md)'s channel. It does not say that every contribution is owed uptake. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-404](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-404.md) v2 | An organization can be governed from outside without any of its decisions being made for it, through the evidence its own procedures receive or through the criteria by which they weigh evidence; the two routes are distinct and each is possible without the other, so informational and evaluative independence do not imply each other; and where the organization's role is to evaluate another that affects its evidence or resources, the interpretation–authority loop can close between the two institutions, so that formal independence of the evaluator's procedure does not make its evaluation independent | The owner's cases, U20 ("maybe cases like reflexive control and regulatory capture could be informative here") and U21 (news-media capture) of the exchange of 2026-10-20, with A26 §4's two constructions and A27 §6. A20: "Control over an organization need not consist in issuing its decisions. It can consist in shaping the conditions under which the organization determines its own decisions". A26: "Neither guarantees the other." [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md) holds the informational half and [CLAIM-348](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md) the evaluative half. The sharp edge: it names possible mechanisms. It does not say that any regulator, newsroom or expert body is captured. The replies' empirical works, read on 2026-10-21, ground the two routes and give nothing to the loop between institutions. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-405](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-405.md) v2 | An individuation is well defined only once its criterion is fixed (the target it serves, the transformations its unity must survive, the scale), and that dependence does not make it arbitrary: once the criterion is fixed a verdict can be false, and differently fixed criteria can pick out units of one system whose boundaries cross rather than nest, none of them less real for it | The individuation counterpart of the owner's normative thesis [CLAIM-363](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md) ("once they are fixed, the judgment can be false"), as A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-20 put it, on the owner's U8 question about "contextuality/relativity/subjectivity". A8 §9: "the underlying system is objectively real, while some scientifically meaningful properties of its descriptions are objectively relational." A9: "an individuation claim can be objectively assessed once its relevant organizational criteria are specified", and "A system may exhibit several objectively grounded forms of unity that need not share the same boundary." [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md) gives the relativity; this claim adds that relativity is not arbitrariness. It bears on QUESTION-065 without answering it. It does not say which criterion is right. | Active |
| [CLAIM-406](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-406.md) v5 | Structural, pre-emptive testimonial injustice has the form of the record's trust loop: an arrangement that decides whose word is sought can keep an early exclusion going through the indicators of competence that only being sought produces, with no continuing prejudiced act; but the loop alone cannot tell perpetuated privilege from merited expertise, because that needs the prejudice condition the dynamics do not contain | The owner's, U24 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on A23's closing thesis: "this seems to me reminiscent of themes in feminist philosophy, e.g. perpetuation of privilege". A24 granted it. [CLAIM-277](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-277.md)'s loop already runs from early advantage to "undeserved authority", and its note of 2026-10-18 from the side that loses. Fricker's un-refreshed list ([THEORY-327](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-327.md)) is a case of it in which some people's views "are not sought". The sharp edge: the loop is the same whether what it entrenches was earned, and only a prejudice makes it an injustice. | Active |
| [CLAIM-407](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md) v3 | A coarse-graining exactly informationally closed under a process's ordinary dynamics need not preserve its responses to an intervention on the mechanism: for a declared intervention distribution ρ, independent of the state, the deficiency Γ = I(S; Y^(I) \| T(S), I) can be positive, as in the hidden governance bit, where it is ρ(h = 1) bits; and Γ = 0 exactly when, for every intervention ρ charges, the response kernels are constant on T's fibres over the states of positive probability | A16 §3–4 of the exchange of 2026-10-20 and A17 §4.2–4.3, its paper's Proposition 1, reused at A18 and in A23's audit. A16: "a representation can be perfectly informationally closed under the ordinary dynamics while failing to preserve a governance-relevant counterfactual distinction." The witness is [CASE-125](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-125.md); the proof is in the body, checked exactly on 2026-10-21. | [CLAIM-410](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-410.md) v3 | Removing a constraint on an organization's members does not move it along one scale of more or less governance: it changes a profile of who holds rule-making, monitoring, enforcement, appeal and revision, in which the authority the constraint held can be eliminated, distributed or transferred, and the members' first-order options and their share in revising the conditions of their action can move in opposite directions | The owner's question, U18 of the exchange of 2026-10-20: "what does this suggest about e.g. "deregulation" as an ideological end?" | [CLAIM-412](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-412.md) v6 | Experience is constituted by interpretive organization, not produced by it: an appropriately organized process in which signals acquire significance for a system is the experience, so whether a system can have experience becomes whether it can sustain that organization | The owner's, U1 and U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-21. | [CLAIM-413](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-413.md) v2 | Grounding is not a property of an experience but a relation among an interpretation, what it purports to be about, and a process that constrains it independently; in its current, developmental and epistemic senses it comes apart from whether the interpretation occurs, so ungrounded is not unconstrained, and what makes an interpretive organization experiential need not be what makes its contents veridical | The owner's premise at U1, that sensory apparatus is necessary for grounded experience, as A1, A3, A5 and A7 restated it. | [CLAIM-417](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-417.md) v4 | What the record explained by "self" in its dispositional, persisting, self-governing and integrated senses is better explained by organizational perspectives, with a perspective, its carriers, its lineage and its representations kept apart; the subject sense stays a separate question, and narrative, presented and modeled selves involve representations that may describe a perspective, attribute it to a bearer or construct an owner, none of them the perspective itself | The owner's, at U31 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the record's earlier "selves" are "better described as 'organizational perspectives'". | [CLAIM-418](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-418.md) v2 | Possessing, enacting or being shaped by an organizational perspective does not establish an independent agent, and perspectival, agential and institutional boundaries need not coincide: several agents can share a perspective, one agent can act through several, and a perspective can be reproduced with no agent governing it; where a perspective contributes to an agent's activity it can enable and constrain the exercise of agency, and that exercise can reproduce or transform it, while whether agency universally requires such a perspective stays open | From the branch of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the owner's question at U38, "what's the relationship between perspective and agency?", A38's answer, and A39's request that it be recorded. | [CLAIM-423](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-423.md) v2 | In a political collective, components that change at different speeds (attention, coalitions, elected terms, administrative careers, law and treaties, generational memory) are not only nested by timescale: under a given institutional arrangement their different temporal horizons affect which forms of influence each can accumulate, exercise and keep, and so which of them holds authority over the others, so a state can stay continuous as an actor while the organization producing its positions changes under it | The owner's, at U28 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: domestic and international politics as the domain where "regime ecology" becomes concrete, with "separation of timescales in elections, durations of tenure in elected and appointed positions, lifespan, generational memory, etc." creating "amorphous collectives of varying orders and degrees of coupling". | [CLAIM-432](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-432.md) v3 | A corporation can be an agent fit to be held responsible and the bearer of functional affect in Frijda's sense, so psychopathy's affective features can be assigned to it as well as its conduct: it lacks remorse, functionally, when harm it does to others is not among the concerns its own appraisals track and gains precedence over what it does only when a regulator or a market turns it into a threat to the corporation's concerns; that profile, threat without remorse, is the construct's, and it is changed by redesigning the corporation's concerns, not its members' characters | The record's reading of Bakan's "institutional psychopath", filed at the owner's request on 2026-10-23 and revised the same day when the owner pointed out that the record's framework assigns affect to corporation-like things ([CLAIM-039](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-039.md), reopened). | [CLAIM-434](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-434.md) | On a finite set of outcomes, some function rises with every move that wins one of a negotiation's conflicts exactly when no chain of winning moves returns to where it began, and the length of the longest such chain ending at an outcome is one such function; a perfectly transitive record of which side won each pair, in a complete tournament contesting every pair once, leaves a cyclic share of (n − 2)/3n under the Hodge decomposition, a baseline that does not carry to sparse records; the Hodge gradient can reverse a comparison the wins settle, netting a record erases alternation, a record fixes a class of potentials rather than one, a coherent record is not yet one aligned with any single perspective's ordering, a best-fitting ordering of a cycle is no Lyapunov function, the sign a class of potentials gives can be set-valued, and an ordering fitted to a record overstates its agreement there | The formal core of the rename of 2026-10-23 from "ascendancy" to "potential" ([TERM-076](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-076.md)). | [CLAIM-436](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-436.md) v3 | An instantaneous ordering is a common currency on a finite set of options, where every complete preorder has a real-valued representation, but not in general: the lexicographic order on the unit square has no real-valued representation, while a continuous complete preorder on a connected separable space has a continuous one; so admitting an ordering is strictly weaker than admitting a currency, a graded lexicographic override lies in the gap while an exact threshold override does not, a threshold override with a discrimination threshold is a lexicographic semiorder whose choices can cycle and so is no ordering at all, and even where each instant has a currency, successive currencies need not share exchange rates | The formal half of the owner's reframing of 2026-10-23, that a "common currency" is better read as a negotiation admitting an (at least instantaneous) ordering. The central experiment, in which physical coupling, correspondence maps and apparatus revision are manipulated independently, is [CASE-179](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-179.md). The open questions it organizes are [QUESTION-282](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-282.md), [QUESTION-283](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-283.md), [QUESTION-285](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-285.md), [QUESTION-281](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md) and [QUESTION-115](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-115.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-475](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-475.md) | Specifying is itself a resource-bounded realization: formulating a question takes time, concepts and computation as realizing a configuration takes energy and matter, so the questions an agent can ask are a product of what it has already realized; a stabilized specification is past inquiry stored so that later questions become cheaper to ask, and it can make other questions harder | The owner's, U17 of the exchange of 2026-10-27: "resource constraints impact specification in exactly the same way as they impact realization. I can't interrogate a question that takes me more time than I have to even ask it." It extends [CLAIM-470](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-470.md): if inquiry is specification, specifying is a process with costs, and the feasible questions are bounded before any answering starts. A17 and A18 drew a consequence the record can use: [TERM-065](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-065.md) takes its query family as supplied, and this claim says that family is the output of bounded activity. A stable specification amortizes the work that made it, which is a separation of time scales ([CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md)), and entrenches what it makes cheap. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-476](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-476.md) v2 | Beyond what it does operationally, luria is an apparatus in Barad's constitutive sense for the objects of a record, and only for them: the record's objects are constituted, and not only made referable and governable, by the distinctions its grammar enacts, so that the same authored material is a different set of objects under a revised apparatus, and the record's own inquiry reconstitutes the apparatus that constitutes them | The owner's, U7 of the exchange of 2026-10-27: "oh shit, I think I may have inadvertently operationalized this notion of apparatus already, check out github.com/dmarx/luria". Split at the owner's review of the pull request. What luria demonstrably does, differentiating, retaining, enforcing and revising the distinctions that fix a record's objects, is now [CLAIM-469](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-469.md), stated without Barad. This claim keeps the further, constitutive thesis: those objects are constituted in Barad's sense, not only made governable. That needs an argument the operational facts do not supply, and the readings press on it, since Barad rejects carrying agential realism as a template. Barad is unread here. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-477](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md) v2 | Relata stand to relations as realizations stand to specifications: what an entity is, is partly fixed by the constraints on the configurations of entities and relations it can enter, and those constraints are themselves realized and maintained by something, so neither relata nor relations, nor specifications nor realizations, are prior without qualification | The owner's, U8 of the exchange of 2026-10-27, "maybe relata:relations::realization:specifications/constraints?", after U6 had set the record's ambitions as "extremely abstract and unrestricted". A8 sharpened it: "Relata are to relational structure somewhat as realizations are to specifications—but relations themselves also have realizations", and added the recursion, that constraints "are themselves realizations within larger relational structures". Filed unrestricted in domain, as the frame of which [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) and [CLAIM-136](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-136.md) are domain cases. It is not a structural realism that eliminates relata, and satisfying a specification is not being produced by it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md) | Scale separation helps make structure and not only marks it: where some degrees of freedom settle fast relative to others, the relation they settle into is a constraint on the system over the window between the two time scales, so what is a realization at one scale works as a constraint at another; and organization can make new separations in turn, as when modes slow near an instability and become order parameters, so time-scale hierarchies and constraints can produce one another | The owner's, U12 of the exchange of 2026-10-27: "I think we may still have a coverage gap wrt scale separation and how that participates in creating structure". A12 agreed and found that the gap was synthesis, not literature: the record held [CLAIM-331](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md), [CLAIM-327](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md), [THEORY-661](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-661.md), [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md) and Mori–Zwanzig readings. It goes beyond [CLAIM-331](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md), on which slowness is a mark of a level, in two ways: separation makes constraints, and constraints can make separation. It supplies the mechanism for [CLAIM-477](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md)'s recursion. It does not say that slowness is sufficient or necessary for a constraint, or that a constraint is an individual. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-479](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-479.md) | In the record a typed relation is more constrained than either of its relata: a claim's content is open prose, while `rests_on` fixes the scheme at both ends, has `supports` written as its converse and says what retiring its target leaves, and none of that moves when either claim's content does; so a relation's rigidity is a fact about the grammar, not evidence that the dependency it records is sound | The owner's, U6 of the exchange of 2026-10-27, against A5's "its relationships are explicitly represented rather than metaphysically primitive": "and yet interestingly, relations like "supports" are less flexible than the raw contents of either relata." Shown from luria.yaml, which A6 §6 read correctly. The relation's type is determinate where the relata's content is not, and that determinacy is no warrant for the dependency: [CLAIM-293](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-293.md) is the demonstrated case. [CASE-131](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-131.md) is the instance in which the rigidity of a relation outran what its relata meant and the grammar was amended. | Active |
| [CLAIM-480](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-480.md) v2 | Composing interactions can turn an interior into a constraint, and sometimes into a constraint of a new kind: in the chain E = ½k₁(x₁ − x₂)² + ½k₂(x₂ − x₃)², with x₂ internal and equilibrated, the boundary sees E_eff = ½·k₁k₂/(k₁ + k₂)·(x₁ − x₃)², a coupling between x₁ and x₃ that neither part has; if the interior relaxes slowly, eliminating it leaves a history-dependent constraint, a memory kernel, so interconnection fixes an effective constraint on the boundary's trajectories and separation of time scales decides only whether that constraint is approximately memoryless; and for cellular sheaves the reduced constraint can relate three boundary values where every relation among the parts is pairwise | From A22 §4 and A23 §IV of the exchange of 2026-10-27, which called composition "the most important missing mechanism" after the owner's U20. Eliminating an equilibrated interior leaves an effective boundary relation that no part has; an outside system interacting only with the boundary meets it as a constraint, and "The interior has effectively become apparatus." Baez and Fong's black-boxing functor is the general theorem for passive linear networks. The memory case ties it to Mori–Zwanzig and to [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md): interconnection yields an effective constraint on the boundary's trajectories in every case, and separation of time scales decides only whether it is approximately memoryless. For cellular sheaves the reduction can need a richer relational vocabulary than the parts used (THEORY-1090; QUESTION-283). It is independent evidence for [CLAIM-477](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md), that constraints are realized by organization. | Active |
| [CLAIM-483](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-483.md) | An argument developed with collaborators who keep no memory fails mainly at identity and not at structure, so that coding what recurs, not argument mapping, is the remedy, and this holds beyond one owner and one assistant family | The comparative and general half of [CLAIM-177](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md) version 1, split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 ([ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md)) and kept Proposed. [CLAIM-177](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md) now says what the record observed: identity failures recurring across six exchanges with one owner and one assistant family. Whether they outnumber structure defects was counted in one exchange only, and the population is one owner and one family, which [CLAIM-177](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md)'s own body called "a pattern, not a measurement". | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-484](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-484.md) | Internal conflict is the gap between the precedence a motive claims over action and the authority the rest of the organization grants it | The second half of [CLAIM-283](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-283.md) version 1, split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 ([ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md)) and kept Proposed. Each of [CLAIM-283](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-283.md)'s four dependents ([CLAIM-368](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-368.md), [CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md), [CLAIM-442](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-442.md), [CLAIM-446](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-446.md)) uses only the first half, the distinction between claimed precedence and granted authority, which is now [CLAIM-283](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-283.md) and is Active. That internal conflict is this gap is a further identification, and no case in the record shows it. [CASE-151](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-151.md) and [CASE-127](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-127.md) illustrate the separation of access from authority, and their notes say they do not show that a motive claimed precedence. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-485](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-485.md) v2 | In the self-governing sense, what endogenous governance adds over a behaviourally equivalent system with an external scheduler is not that it allocates authority among its own processes but that it can revise its own governing standards when they break down | The bridge the owner asked for on 2026-10-28, between Kahl's proposal (THEORY-1165), which is about agency in the sense that bears on responsibility, and [QUESTION-092](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-092.md), which fixes [TERM-045](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-045.md)'s sense 5, self-governing. It is the record's answer to the question. Internal allocation of authority, the second of [CLAIM-025](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-025.md)'s separable capacities (governing among regimes), coordinates execution and does not make a system govern itself more than an external scheduler would. The capacity to revise its governing standards when they break down does: the third capacity, which [CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md) names as taking part in governing the conditions of its own transformation. Two systems matched within a regime differ under it, and they diverge in behaviour once that regime breaks down. | Active |
| [CLAIM-486](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-486.md) | A rendering can keep the communicative act while changing the proposition, so preserving the proposition is not necessary for preserving the communicative event | The necessity half of [CLAIM-061](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-061.md)'s version 1, split off when the status review of 2026-10-28 narrowed [CLAIM-061](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-061.md) to sufficiency ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s third ruling). Its one documented case is Phillips's handshake for Paul's holy kiss ([CASE-056](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-056.md)), which competent judges took to keep the greeting. The defender of necessity has a reply the record does not answer: the proposition worth keeping is the coarser one, and the handshake keeps it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-487](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-487.md) | Describing the relations that decide which regime becomes effective as one will-organization, across realizers, explains something that planning theory, control theory, executive-control research and institutional theory each describing their own realizer does not | The explanatory-gain claim the paper stakes itself on, filed separately by the status review of 2026-10-28. It was carried by [CLAIM-027](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-027.md)'s standing without being one of its words, so [CLAIM-024](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-024.md)'s objection had no target of its own. [CLAIM-021](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-021.md) concedes the mechanisms; this is what is left to show: that one description across realizers earns its keep. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-488](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-488.md) | Le Cam deficiency, after Torgersen, would quantify the approximate case of the Blackwell order for translation, and decoder-only audience knowledge would make the coding problem a Wyner-Ziv problem | The two steps of the manuscript's §5 that [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md) carried until the status review of 2026-10-28 and that rest on works the record has not read: deficiency for the approximate case (Torgersen) and the Wyner-Ziv form of decoder side information. Split off when [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md) was narrowed to what its read sources support ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s third ruling). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-489](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-489.md) v2 | A sign's communicative significance is fixed by its contrasts within a system rather than by correspondence to a referent | [CLAIM-082](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-082.md)'s version 1 title, kept as its own Proposed entry when the sixth status review narrowed [CLAIM-082](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-082.md) to what Saussure's value supports ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s third ruling). It carries the two parts the reading does not: that significance in use is fixed this way, and that contrast works instead of reference rather than alongside it. | Rejected |
| [CLAIM-490](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-490.md) | A fanbase is a mixture of spectators who relate to the club in different ways, as supporters, followers, fans and flâneurs, so the public stance credited to it is weighted towards the most committed types before any bias in who is sampled | From Giulianotti's taxonomy ([THEORY-1111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1111.md)): supporters are hot and bound to the club as community, while flâneurs are cool consumers who switch clubs. The expressions that make up "the fans hate the owner" come from the hot types, and the cool ones take no part. So the stance is the committed segment's by composition, before amplification or preference falsification. It does not say the committed segment is a minority, or that its stance is illegitimate. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-491](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-491.md) | No action is selfless in the sense of aiming at a good that is no self's: what is called selflessness, collectivist or altruistic, is concern for the good of a self extended to include others or a group, so collectivism is self-interest on a larger self-identity | The owner's position, from the discussion that raised self-categorization theory (2026-10-28 and 29). Selves come at more and less inclusive levels: social identity in self-categorization theory, fusion, self-expansion, interdependent self-construal. Apparent selflessness is then concern for a larger self. Cialdini et al.'s "oneness" result is its best evidence; Batson et al.'s rejoinder and the risk of trivial truth are its objections. It does not say people are self-centred, or that groups have no good of their own. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-493](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-493.md) | When a fanbase is set against an outside party such as its club's owner, its more extreme members become more prototypical of it, so a vocal minority can fix the fanbase's public stance through a group process and not only through biased sampling of who speaks | A derivation from self-categorization theory: in an intergroup context the more extreme members of a group gain prototypicality (Turner et al. 1994, p. 458, reporting Haslam and Turner). If influence follows prototypicality (Turner 2005, unread), a fanbase opposed to its owner will treat its most hostile members as most representative. A minority stance can then become the fanbase's public stance by a group process that A2's preference falsification and amplification do not need. It does not say that the private majority agrees. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-495](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-495.md) | For an O(d)-valued connection on a connected graph, the assignments that meet every edge relation xᵢ = Tᵢⱼxⱼ form a space isomorphic to the vectors at one vertex fixed by every holonomy based there, which is the kernel of the connection Laplacian; for d = 1, and for U(1) phases, that space is all or nothing, but for d > 1 a connection whose loops are not trivial can still keep a subspace on which every loop is, so compatibility among local frames can be partial and graded by direction; and edge maps that do not commute can compose to a flat loop, so non-commutativity is not holonomy | From A2 and A3 of the exchange "Paper assessment" (2026-10-29), which drew it out of [LIT-1820](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1820.md)'s O(d) setting against [THEORY-1082](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1082.md)'s U(1) one. The proof and the example are the record's, checked numerically. It is the zeroth cohomology of the connection sheaf, so standard, and it says nothing about which organizations have such transports. | Active |
| [CLAIM-496](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-496.md) | Agreement between routes of translation is a measure of coherence, not of fidelity, and the two are independent: a rendering that sends every source utterance to one output makes direct and relay transport agree exactly while a receiver who could tell a promise from a prediction with no error is left at chance, and two routes that keep the act and differ in register disagree completely while losing nothing the act-identification task needs | From A4 and A5 of the exchange "Paper assessment" (2026-10-29), where the assistant carried [LIT-1820](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1820.md)'s comparison of alternative paths over to translation and then warned that "path agreement is a coherence criterion, not a fidelity criterion". The constructions are the record's. It does not say path discrepancy is uninformative: it says it measures something [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md)'s directed loss does not, and conversely. | Active |
